subject: Tell your state legislators: Don’t strip these key environmental protections
snippet:
Soham,

We are at risk of losing critical environmental protections.

A new law overturned California’s bedrock environmental law, the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Now, companies can fast-track major projects without review—threatening endangered species’ habitats, stripping protections from conserved lands, and increasing pollution risks to public health.

Tell your state legislators you do not want to lose the environmental protections that make our state great.

For decades, commonsense rules have limited the impact of industrial development on our basic environmental needs: clean water, clean air, and open space. But, Assembly Bill/Senate Bill 131, which was hurriedly passed this summer, has put these valuable protections in danger.

Normally, proposed projects on state land need to undergo environmental review to ensure that the health of our communities and the endangered animals who live there won’t be adversely affected. This bill torpedoes that requirement, circumventing the vital review process to accelerate industrial development.

With risky broad exemptions and dangerous new allowances, the law’s vague definitions allow for “advanced manufacturing” factories to be exempted from environmental review and zoned for industrial use. This could mean any factory that uses AI could be exempt. It could also mean facilities housing defense and aerospace manufacturing, metal and plastic processing, fuel production, and more than 60 other polluting industries can evade environmental review.

We’re calling on the California legislature to fix these glaring oversteps. Tell your representative: Communities’ health is not a fair trade-off for rushed development.

While AB/SB 131 aimed to streamline industrial development, we cannot lose protections that prevent industrial development from polluting our communities and paving over the homes of endangered species like mountain lions, desert tortoises or burrowing owls.

This week, we have a rare opportunity to undo the negative impact of this law and regain protections for our environment, our health, and our endangered species. Take action by telling your state legislators to safeguard our hard-won environmental protections.

Thanks,


Jake Twomey
CALPIRG Students

subject: Update your voter registration today!

Voting is at the heart of any strong democracy. Today is National Voter Registration Day and if you are eligible to vote, it's a great opportunity to make sure that your voter registration status is up-to-date so you are ready to vote in the upcoming elections.

You can register for the first time or update your registration status right here.

As the largest and most diverse generation alive right now, young people have a chance to make a real impact in our country if every eligible voter participates in elections. In order to make sure that you can raise your voice and cast your vote in the upcoming local, state, and federal elections, you need to be registered to vote at your current address.

We know a lot of students recently moved for the start of the school year. If you need to register for the first time or you moved since you last registered, you can update your registration right here.

Voting Resources: Check your voter registration status and find out more about upcoming elections, including how to vote by mail.

Happy voting!

Jake Twomey
